verifications.claim: The International Day of Happiness is observed annually on March 20.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The International Day of Happiness is celebrated throughout the world on 20 March." (R1); "Observed each year on March 20" (R2); "Every year on March 20th" (R3); "every year on March 20th" (R4); "March 20th is the UN International Day of Happiness" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the annual observance on March 20.

verifications.claim: The International Day of Happiness is a United Nations-established day.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "established by the United Nations General Assembly" (R1); "established by the United Nations in 2012" (R2); "the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution" (R3); "The United Nations declared" (R4); "a United Nations project" (R5)

verifications.claim: The International Day of Happiness recognizes happiness and well-being as universal goals and priorities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "pursuit of happiness is a fundamental human goal" "promotes sustainable development, poverty eradication, happiness and the well-being of all peoples" (R1); "well-being, not just economic growth, should be a global priority" (R2); "increase happiness and wellbeing" (R3); "promote happiness, well-being" (R4); "happiness is a basic human right" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly link the day to recognizing happiness and well-being as goals.

verifications.claim: The International Day of Happiness promotes a "happiness for all" agenda.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "happiness and the well-being of all peoples" (R1); "Happiness as a fundamental human right and goal for all" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Sources promote happiness universally but do not use exact "happiness for all" phrase.

verifications.claim: 2026 events for the International Day of Happiness focus on social media's impact and intentional offline connection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "focuses on the connection between social media and well-being" "taking breaks from social media or using it more intentionally" (R2); "explores the relationship between social media and happiness" "healthier, more intentional relationship with social media" "analogue activities" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: 2026-specific sources directly describe focus on social media impact and intentional/offline alternatives.

verifications.claim: The date of the International Day of Happiness is March 20th of every year.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "20 March" "FrequencyAnnual" (R1); "each year on March 20" (R2); "Every year on March 20th" (R3); "every year on March 20th" (R4); "20th March 2026" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of annual March 20 date across sources.

verifications.claim: The International Day of Happiness was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2012.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "established by the United Nations General Assembly on 28 June 2012" (R1); "established by the United Nations in 2012" (R2); "UN General Assembly adopted a resolution stating International Happiness Day would be celebrated every year on March 20th" (R3); "The United Nations declared March 20th as the International Day of Happiness in 2012" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on UN General Assembly and 2012 year.

verifications.claim: The establishment of the International Day of Happiness followed a proposal from UN adviser Jayme Illien.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In 2011, Jayme Illien proposed the idea of the International Day of Happiness" (R1); "In 2011, a UN adviser called Jayme Illien suggested the idea" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Jayme Illien's proposal led to establishment.

verifications.claim: Jayme Illien's proposal was to promote a "happiness for all" agenda.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Illien's proposal as promoting happiness economics or increasing happiness, but no "happiness for all" agenda.

verifications.claim: The 2026 focus of the International Day of Happiness is "Happiness and Social Media".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "SOCIAL MEDIA & HAPPINESS" "This year’s theme explores the relationship between social media and happiness"
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly titles 2026 theme as "SOCIAL MEDIA & HAPPINESS", matching closely.

verifications.claim: The 2026 focus of the International Day of Happiness explores how social media impacts well-being, especially for young people.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "focuses on the connection between social media and well-being" "happiness among young people has declined" "teens who use social platforms" (R2); "relationship between social media and happiness, highlighting the potential challenges for our wellbeing" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: 2026 sources cover social media's impact on well-being, with R2 specifying young people.

verifications.claim: The 2026 focus of the International Day of Happiness encourages mindful use or breaks from social media.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "taking breaks from social media or using it more intentionally" (R2); "Be mindful of if, when and how much you are on social media" "try a ‘digital sabbath’" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for mindful use and breaks in 2026 context.

verifications.claim: The World Happiness Report is typically released around March 20.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Data from the World Happiness Report will be released" (on March 20 context, R2); "published on 19 March 2026" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate release around March 20, as in 2026 example.
